title: Change of rings preserves K-flat complexes with flat terms
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site and $\varphi:\mathcal O\to\mathcal O'$ a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. Let $\mathcal K^\bullet$ be a K-flat complex of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-kflat-complex] whose terms $\mathcal K^p$ are flat $\mathcal O$-modules (the functor $-\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal K^p$ on $\mathcal O$-modules is exact). Then the complex $\mathcal K^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'$, obtained by applying the change of rings $-\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] termwise, is a K-flat complex of $\mathcal O'$-modules whose terms are flat $\mathcal O'$-modules.

proof.text: Write $R=\mathcal O$, $S=\mathcal O\prime$, and $U=\varphi_*$ for restriction of scalars. This leaves the underlying abelian sheaf and maps unchanged. Kernels are sectionwise and cokernels are sheafified sectionwise cokernels in both module categories, so their underlying abelian sheaves agree before and after $U$. Thus $U$ preserves and reflects exactness, and for every complex $F$ the underlying abelian sheaves of $H^i(UF)$ and $H^i(F)$ coincide; in particular $U$ preserves and reflects acyclicity.

proof.text: For any $R$-module sheaf $M$ and $S$-module sheaf $N$, construct an isomorphism of $R$-module sheaves $U(N\otimes_S(M\otimes_R S))\cong UN\otimes_R M$. On local tensor generators send $n\otimes(m\otimes s)$ to $sn\otimes m$ and send $n\otimes m$ back to $n\otimes(m\otimes1)$. The first formula respects the inner $R$-balancing since $s\varphi(r)n\otimes m=sn\otimes rm$, and the outer $S$-balancing since $tn\otimes(m\otimes s)$ and $n\otimes(m\otimes ts)$ both map to $tsn\otimes m$. The second formula is $R$-balanced because $\varphi(r)n\otimes(m\otimes1)=n\otimes(m\otimes\varphi(r))=n\otimes(rm\otimes1)$. Give $UN\otimes_R M$ its $S$-action on the $N$ factor: on presheaf tensors $t(n\otimes m)=tn\otimes m$, and module sheafification extends this action. To construct the first sheaf map, first extend the $R$-bilinear map $N\times(M\otimes_{p,R}S)\to UN\otimes_R M$ by the cited bilinear-extension theorem over $R$. Its $S$-balancing and $S$-linearity hold on the presheaf tensors by the displayed formulas and therefore on the sheafifications by uniqueness of extension (also on each localized site to test a local section of $S$). The tensor and sheafification universal properties over $S$ then give the first map. The second formula is an $R$-bilinear map into the restricted left-hand sheaf, so the tensor and sheafification universal properties over $R$ give the inverse map. Their composites are the identity: $sn\otimes(m\otimes1)=n\otimes(m\otimes s)$, and $1n\otimes m=n\otimes m$. Uniqueness of extension makes these identities identities of sheaf maps. Both maps are natural in $M$ and $N$.

proof.text: Fix $p$ and a short exact sequence of $S$-module sheaves. By step 1 its restriction to $R$ is exact. Apply the exact functor $-\otimes_R K^p$, exact by the termwise flatness hypothesis, and then identify the resulting sequence with the restriction of its tensor product over $S$ with $K^p\otimes_R S$ using the natural maps of step 2. Reflection of exactness in step 1 proves that $-\otimes_S(K^p\otimes_R S)$ is exact. This proves flatness of each changed term.

source.place: Tag 05V4, label lemma-flat-change-of-rings, proof with the module denoted H on the left also on the right

proof.text: For an arbitrary complex $F$ of $S$-module sheaves, apply step 2 to $N=F^a$, $M=K^b$, and take direct sums over $a+b=n$. Restriction of scalars commutes with these sums: the underlying sheaf is the sheafification of sectionwise finite-support tuples; scalar action is componentwise through $\varphi$, so sheafifying and restricting in either order gives the same sheaf. The sheafification adjunction verifies its coproduct universal property by maps from each summand. We obtain $U\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes_S(K\otimes_R S))\cong\operatorname{Tot}(UF\otimes_R K)$. This is a chain isomorphism: the formula $f\otimes(k\otimes s)\mapsto sf\otimes k$ sends the two differential terms to $s\,d_Ff\otimes k$ and $(-1)^a sf\otimes d_Kk$, respectively, exactly the total differential on the right. Every sum here uses finite-support representatives locally; no boundedness hypothesis is needed.

proof.text: Now let $F$ be any acyclic complex of $S$-module sheaves. Step 1 makes $UF$ acyclic. By K-flatness of $K$, the complex $\operatorname{Tot}(UF\otimes_R K)$ is acyclic. The chain isomorphism of step 4 and reflection of acyclicity in step 1 make $\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes_S(K\otimes_R S))$ acyclic. This is precisely the definition of K-flatness over $S$. Together with step 3 it proves both conclusions.
